entities.summary:
Ashipa was a prominent economist and social scientist of the Benin Empire during the Classical era. Born in an unknown year, Ashipa lived and died in 1716. He was a key figure associated with the monarchs and rulers of the Benin Empire, known for his work in understanding the intricacies of statecraft and imperial administration.

Ashipa's contributions were instrumental in shaping the economic and social structures of the Benin Empire, which at its peak spanned over 300,000 square miles. His work on taxation, trade, and diplomacy helped to establish the empire as a major power in West Africa.

Despite the empire's eventual decline, Ashipa's ideas continued to influence the development of West African societies, with many of his theories on statecraft and imperial administration being adopted by other kingdoms and empires.

One of Ashipa's most lasting legacies is the establishment of the Benin Empire's system of taxation, which remains in use to this day in parts of West Africa.

As Ashipa once said, 'A strong empire is built on the backs of its people, and a wise ruler knows when to let go.'
